title: Hosted API Embeddings + Rerank Demo — ZenithSearch
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked ZenithSearch through the Hosted API embeddings + rerank flow: embedding ingestion, vector search, and server-side reranking via the rerank endpoint. Discussed expected latency, batching, and cost levers, plus security (SOC2, KMS, VPC options) and next steps to run a pilot and a benchmark using ZenithSearch sample dataset.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-17
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (ZenithSearch Head of Search), Tom Elliot (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (ML Eng)

---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm maya from redwood -- i'll run quick intro and then liam will jump into the demo. how's everyone's afternoon?
[00:10] Aisha: good thanks, busy week but excited. we kicked off this because search relevance is our main open problem, so looking forward.
[00:15] Maya: great — quick agenda, show hosted embeddings flow, vector search, then our rerank endpoint which lets you do server-side cross-attention reranking, talk cost/latency tradeoffs and security, and close with next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Tom: yep, please include any notes about VPC/priv deployments, we have compliance questions.
[00:34] Liam: absolutely, we'll cover hosted first and mention dedicated/private options.

Summary & context gathering:
[00:45] Maya: can you give a bit of context — traffic, qps, latency targets, and what you use today?
[00:51] Aisha: sure — we serve about 150 qps peak across search, avg p95 around 750ms now, we want p95 under 300ms for late 2027, and relevance lift is the top priority; we currently use elastic with a hybrid BM25+semantic pipeline. embeddings are precomputed and stored in an external vector store, we were testing Pinecone last quarter.
[01:15] Priya: budget is a concern — we need to show 2-3x improvement in metrics at reasonable cost, also encryption at rest and audit logs required.
[01:24] Maya: good — that'll help frame the demo.

Demo start (technical walkthrough):
[01:35] Liam: okay opening the console — note i'm on the hosted account. first, our embeddings endpoint: you can POST documents or batch vectors, we support streaming and chunking. here's a sample payload — i'll run a small demo against sample docs.
[01:52] [01:52] Liam: (typing) run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '@sample.json' --api-key XXX — returns ids + vectors.
[02:05] Liam: so typical latency for small batch (16 docs) is ~120-160ms on our hosted line for embeddings, for larger models it goes up. note these are per-request times; you can do batching to amortize cost.
[02:19] Tom: that's pretty tight. how are vectors stored? are you recommending an external vector DB or Redwood-managed store?
[02:26] Liam: for hosted we offer a managed vector store that we integrate with for reranking pipelines; you can also push vectors to your store like pinecone or an open-source option. our rerank endpoint can accept candidate ids with embeddings or raw texts.
[02:40] Priya: so flow would be: embed query, run ANN in our managed store or your chosen store, get top-K, then send to rerank endpoint that does cross-encoder scoring?
[02:50] Liam: exactly. the rerank endpoint performs cross-attention over the query and candidates, returned as a scored list. Example: POST /v1/rerank with { query, candidates: [{id, text, embedding?}] } — result sorted with scores + explanation.
[03:07] Aisha: curious about latency — cross-encoder reranks are expensive. what's p50/p95 for a top-10 rerank?
[03:12] Liam: on hosted default model, top-10 rerank p50 ~210ms, p95 ~480ms. those are with batching disabled; if you enable batch windows or small latency SLOs we can push down p95 by concurrent optimization. Also we do prefix/K-V caching for hot queries which helps tail.
[03:34] Tom: realistic numbers. and cost? like token cost for rerank?
[03:39] Liam: cost is model+compute dependent — for SERVER-SUBSET models we show token-equivalent pricing; practical way is we provide an estimate based on your query length and candidate sizes. we'll send sample math.

Transcription artifact (mis-hear / filler):
[03:55] Maya: (laughs) sometimes folks call it the 're-ranker machine' — redwood optim- uh optimize has a profiling tool — we call it Redwood Optimize, but i know docs sometimes say Redwood Optimise in older decks.

Deep dive: rerank behaviour and tuning
[04:08] Liam: key knobs: candidate size (k), context window (truncate or summarize long docs), model variant (smaller cross-encoders for latency), quantized models for lower cost, and route policy — e.g., route to cheaper model during non-peak. We also have a streaming rerank preview if you want partial scores.
[04:30] Priya: what about hallucination / safety in rerank? we rely on factual grounding for answers.
[04:36] Liam: rerank by itself is scoring, not generation, but the model can still favor fluency — we encourage using extracted snippets and conservative candidate pruning; integration tests in evals help. We include quality monitoring in Redwood Console to detect regressions.

Security & compliance
[04:55] Maya: Aisha you mentioned audit logs and encryption?
[04:58] Aisha: yes we need SOC2 level auditability, SSO, and KMS for customer-managed keys.
[05:04] Liam: we support SOC2 compliance on hosted, SAML/SSO and RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. for regulated customers we offer Private (VPC) or on-prem packages with a private control plane. We can send the security whitepaper.
[05:20] Tom: and data residency? some EU data needs to stay in-region.
[05:24] Maya: hosted has region controls and data residency options, or Private deployment if you need full on-prem. We'll include region availability in the follow-up.

Live example: rerank call
[05:40] Liam: i'll walk through a small demo — query: "best way to reset password" and candidates are short KB articles. calling rerank now.
[05:50] [05:50] Liam: (runs API) request payload: {"query":"how do i reset my password?","candidates":[{"id":1,"text":"Resetting your password via settings..."},{"id":2,"text":"Password resets require contacting support..."}]}
[06:05] [06:06] Liam: response: reordered candidates with scores 0.92, 0.37 plus explanation tokens. you can see cross-attention highlights in the explanation field (may be noisy in auto-transcript).
[06:18] Priya: nice. can we get token-level breakdown for cost and latency?
[06:22] Liam: yes that's in the console under per-request analytics. it shows token counts, model used, latency breakdown and cost estimate.

Tradeoffs discussion:
[06:35] Aisha: our expected QPS is spiky — how to control cost during peaks but keep low latency?
[06:42] Liam: common pattern, hybrid routing: route warm traffic to cheaper model or cached responses, reserve dedicated capacity for critical routes, and use autoscaling policies. For hosted we have burst capacity and you can set fallback policies so if the primary reranker is saturated we fall back to a lighter model or a heuristic score.
[07:02] Tom: do you recommend managing your own vector DB for scale?
[07:05] Liam: if you already have an optimized ANN store, you can keep it. Our managed store simplifies operations and offers tighter integration for rerank batching and candidate retrieval. We'll share benchmark sheets comparing throughput.

Benchmarks & pilot plan
[07:20] Maya: next step we usually do a 2-week pilot: we run sample dataset A/B against your current pipeline, measure relevance metrics and latency, and then iterate. We'll provision trial keys and a small dedicated pool if needed.
[07:33] Aisha: that sounds good. timeline-wise we need results before end-of-quarter.
[07:37] Maya: we can do that, aim to start next week.

Questions and clarifications (typical call noise):
[07:45] Priya: quick Q — does rerank accept embeddings-only (i.e. no text) for candidates?
[07:49] Liam: yes, you can send embeddings and we will rehydrate or do an embedding-similarity + lightweight scoring flow; we recommend sending text for explainability.
[07:58] Tom: any client libraries? we saw a python SDK in the docs.
[08:01] Maya: yes Python/Go/JS — sample snippets in the repo. we'll attach them in follow-up.

Wrap-up and next steps recap:
[08:12] Maya: recap — we'll send pricing, security docs, trial api keys, sample scripts and a suggested pilot plan. Liam will share the security deck and benchmark comparison sheet. Aisha/Priya to share dataset and target queries. We'll schedule a pilot kickoff; maya to send calendar invite.
[08:28] Aisha: perfect, thanks both.
[08:31] Tom: thanks, very helpful.
[08:33] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up by Friday.

Notes on transcript quality: some auto-captions glitched on technical acronyms (K-V cache became K-V cash in earlier lines), and names occasionally misattributed. we've cleaned obvious mis-labels but left natural speech noise.
